title: Foundations
description: Start with the basics: what AI is, how it differs from ML and generative AI, and why it matters right now.
goals: Understand the difference between AI, ML, and Generative AI
Learn how large language models work at a high level
Identify what AI is genuinely good and bad at
Recognize where AI already shows up in daily life
tip: Start a simple observation log: every time you encounter AI this week, note what it did and whether it was helpful.

title: Foundations Continued
description: Explore the AI tools landscape and learn how to choose the right tool for the task.
goals: Survey the major AI chatbots and what makes each unique
Understand image, audio, video, and code-generation tools
Learn how to quickly evaluate a new AI tool
Distinguish between free and paid features for beginners
tip: Pick one primary chatbot and stick with it for the whole week — switching constantly slows your learning.

title: Key Concepts
description: Go deeper on how large language models work under the hood.
goals: Understand what tokens are and why they matter for limits and costs
Learn how context windows affect AI memory and behavior
Discover what temperature controls and when to adjust it
Explain why different models behave differently on the same prompt
tip: Experiment with the temperature setting in your chosen chatbot — low values give focused answers, high values give creative ones.

title: Key Concepts Continued
description: Understand why AI confidently makes things up and build habits to catch it before it causes problems.
goals: Recognize why hallucination is a fundamental property of LLMs, not a bug
Identify the different types and levels of hallucination
Know when hallucination is most dangerous
Practice a practical verification habit for everyday use
tip: Always fact-check any AI claim that involves names, dates, statistics, or quotes — treat AI as a helpful editor, not a trusted source.

title: Tools In Depth
description: Get to know the major AI chatbots in detail and understand which excels at what.
goals: Master ChatGPT features, strengths, and best-use scenarios
Learn Claude's advantages for long documents and careful reasoning
Compare models for your specific needs
Decide when upgrading from free to paid is worth it
tip: Keep a one-page comparison sheet of your top three tools, updated whenever you discover a new feature.

title: Tools In Depth Continued
description: Use AI for research and writing without losing your critical thinking or your voice.
goals: Use AI to research topics faster while keeping fact-checking habits sharp
Accelerate writing without sounding robotic
Edit, rewrite, and adjust tone with AI help
Preserve your voice when using AI assistance
tip: When writing with AI, write your own rough draft first, then ask AI to improve specific sections — never start from a blank page and AI alone.

title: Advanced Prompting
description: Go beyond basic prompts and master techniques that dramatically improve AI output quality.
goals: Apply chain-of-thought prompting to improve reasoning tasks
Use few-shot examples to show the AI exactly what you want
Deploy role-play and persona prompting for consistent styles
Combine multiple techniques for complex tasks
tip: Save your best prompts in a personal library — the best prompt engineers reuse and refine proven patterns.

title: Advanced Prompting Continued
description: Turn one-off AI interactions into repeatable, reliable workflows you can run in minutes.
goals: Define what an AI workflow is and why it saves time
Chain prompts together for multi-step tasks
Build reusable prompt templates for common scenarios
Format outputs for structured, consistent results
tip: Design your first workflow around a real task you do every week — like summarizing meeting notes or drafting a status update.

title: Automation and Agents
description: Learn how to automate repetitive tasks using AI tools, no-code platforms, and simple workflows.
goals: Understand what AI automation is and how it differs from scripting
Explore no-code tools: Zapier, Make, and n8n
Build your first automated AI workflow
Identify which tasks in your work are good automation candidates
tip: Start with one small automation this week — even a simple email-to-task flow will show you what is possible.

title: Automation and Agents Continued
description: Understand what AI agents are, how they work, and when they are useful — without writing a single line of code.
goals: Distinguish between a chatbot and an AI agent
Explain how agents use tools, memory, and planning
Explore real use cases: research agents, personal assistants, coding agents
Recognize the risks and limitations of autonomous AI agents
tip: Try one agent-powered workflow this week, but always keep a human-in-the-loop for anything important.

title: Capstone
description: Design your own combination of AI tools and workflows tailored to your work, life, and goals.
goals: Evaluate AI tools for your specific needs and constraints
Build a personal AI toolkit that fits your work
Avoid tool overload and stay focused on what matters
Create a simple review plan for updating your stack over time
tip: Cap your toolkit at five core tools for now — you can always add more, but focus beats breadth.

title: Capstone Continued
description: AI moves fast. Learn how to stay informed without feeling overwhelmed and build a sustainable learning habit.
goals: Identify the best sources for staying current with AI without overwhelm
Filter signal from noise in AI news
Build a sustainable, low-friction AI learning habit
Adopt a confident mindset for navigating a fast-moving field
tip: Pick one 15-minute weekly ritual — a newsletter, a podcast episode, or a research paper skim — and protect that time like a meeting.
